text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Foreign Minister Pavol Hamzik said there was still chance a for Slovakia to be included in the first wave of post-communist countries that will be accepted to NATO.
- Hamzik said Slovakia's problem in foreign policy was that the country's image abroad was worse than the real situation.
- The Slovak subsidiary of telecom equipment producer Ericsson said it wanted to become the leading supplier in the field of mobile and public telecommunication networks.
- Slovak potato production is expected to total 518,719 tonnes this year, exceeding the country's domestic consumption by 110,619 tonnes.
- Czech-based Banka Hana said it planned to open another five offices in Slovakia by the end of this year, under its strategy of expanding its activities over all of Slovakia.
- Slovakia's largest commercial bank VUB said it was close to signing the framework credit lines with German's Berliner Bank AG and Commerzbank AG.

- Sales of shares from the portfolio of the National Property Fund, the state's privatisation agency, on the Slovak capital market totalled around 963 million crowns in the first half of this year. Sales on the O-T-C RM-System bourse accounted for around 95 percent of the overall amount.

- Local authorities in the eastern Slovak town of Revuca have ruled that a controversal monument commemorating the 1,100th anniversary of the arrival of Hungarian tribes to central Europe, will be pulled down. Protests of ethnic Hungarians in the region are expected.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Steel producer VSZ posted an after-tax profit of around 1.5 billion crowns in the first eight months of this year, 277 million more than planned.
- VSZ President Jan Smerek said the increase of the company's holdings in IRB bank over the current 14.63 percent will not threaten the banking sector, nor the state itself.
- Engineering company SES Tlmace, which makes equipment for the energy sector, said its 1996 gross profit should be 60 million crowns, compared with losses of 666 million last year.
- SES said it was preparing projects for oil refiner Slovnaft and cellulose and paper producer SCP Ruzomberok.

SME - Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar rejected information in the Czech media that Slovakia was not repaying the alleged debt of 24 billion crowns to its former federation partner. Meciar said Slovakia did not owe anything to Czech Republic.
